what_changed: Carry-forward fixes on every forecast-check hit (Kilian 11-17). The Q3 10-Q (filed 11-04) shows the Devices segment margin at 32.7% in Q3, not the 33.8% the set had estimated from the release: cost of products sold rose to 33.3% of sales from 32.8% in H1 as CGM price cuts abroad began early. The Devices margin is now built from its three cost lines: product cost at the Q3 ratio (CEO: further CGM price concessions offset by COGS programs; no recovery assumed), R&D growing with sales (CEO: R&D is never cut), SG&A growing at 0.90x sales (FY2024-26 range 0.75-0.93x, launch spending in 2027), and the 2028 Medicare CGM price reset charged with no cost relief. FY2027-29 Devices margin 33.6/33.6/33.8% (was 34.4/34.6/34.8%, a +0.2pt a year carried step). CGM FY2029 +4.0% (the 2028 bid reset is one-time, then CPI updates; FY2027 share gains annualize), EPD FY2029 +6.76% from the emerging-markets mix, core Diagnostics rebuilt by category (Core Lab +5%, Rapid and Molecular +1%). The Q3 segment split now uses the 10-Q for all segments (corporate -203); the other segments' later quarters are not re-based (net ~+$50M EBIT a year, not booked). Growth term x1.0021. Research target (12m) base 109.44 -> 107.73 (-1.6%). Citation-gate fix (2026-11-18): every forward path the gate flagged is now built from real drivers. Electrophysiology grows with its market (about 15% in 2026 per Boston Scientific and Medtronic, 11.5% a year long-range) plus Abbott share from the Volt, TactiFlex Duo and Japan launches: +15% / +12% / +11.5% for FY2027-29 (FY2029 was +10%). Other Devices is built by category (pacemakers +9%, heart failure +6%, vascular +5%, structural heart +6%, neuromodulation flat as Abbott loses share): about +6% a year. Core Lab grows +5% (in line with Roche, with China price cuts as a drag) and rapid and molecular tests +2%. Exact Sciences' cancer tests grow +13% in FY2027 and +11% after as blood tests take part of the screening market. Established Pharma grows +6.5% (the CEO's 7.5-8% record less currency). Nutrition grows +2.3%, which is what the CFO's 'remaining Abbott grows 50-100bp faster after the spin' implies. Diagnostics, Nutrition and Established Pharma margins are rebuilt from their cost lines on the filed Q3 10-Q (they had still used the old estimate). Corporate costs are rebuilt from stock compensation (1.5% of sales) and corporate functions; the corporate-functions level has no forward driver and is a card for Kilian (-$157M, -$260M booked as placeholder, or -$422M a year). Q4 2026 corporate is set from the Q4 EPS guide midpoint, declared and flagged as a last-resort guide use. Net debt now comes from the filed Q3 balance sheet ($26.9B), so the September DOJ payment and part of the NEC settlement are no longer counted twice. Consensus sources were refreshed; the peer P/E median is unchanged at 16.8x and the exit P/E moves to 17.6x. Research target (12m) base 108.15 -> 107.12 (-1.0%). GATE FIX ROUND 2 (2026-11-18): Q4 2026 is no longer set from Abbott's Q4 EPS guide. Each segment's Q4 sales now come from what management said on the Q3 call (EP about 20%, diabetes low to mid single digits) or from its own evidence, and corporate costs from their parts, so Q4 adjusted EPS comes out at $1.49, below the $1.62-1.67 guide (full year $5.37 vs $5.50-5.55, sales growth about 5.5% vs the ~6% guide). Nutrition is now built by product and region: Abbott won Florida's WIC formula contract in February 2026 and loses Michigan's from November 2026, US births are slightly down, older-adult demand grows, and currencies are taken at today's rates; it grows about 0.3% in 2027 and 1.8% a year after. Rapid and molecular tests are built from Roche's matching business lines and the point-of-care market (-1.5% a year), Established Pharma currency from today's exchange rates (-1.3% in 2027, none after), and corporate functions grow with the Fed's inflation projection. Quarters are now split using three years of history adjusted for growth. Litigation and other adjustments are corrected to -$2.0B (-$1.16 a share). Abbott's own EV/EBITDA multiple is recomputed on the September balance sheet and the rebuilt forecast: 14.4x (was 13.3x). Four choices go to Kilian as cards: how large the 2028 Medicare price cut on Libre is, which US and international Libre growth rates to use for 2028-29, Neuromodulation growth, and the cost-ratio path for Diagnostics, Nutrition and Established Pharma; the corporate-cost card is withdrawn because that line is now sourced. Research target (12m) base 107.12 -> 109.78 (+2.5%), mostly from the higher EV/EBITDA multiple. GATE FIX ROUND 3 (2026-11-18): The share of US CGM spending that Medicare pays is now about 21% (Medicare's $1.3B in 2023 against Mordor's $6.28B US market for 2025; no matching-year figure exists, so this is low confidence), so the 2028 Medicare price cut on Libre is 0.83% of CGM sales instead of 1%; the larger 2.5% option is dropped because nothing supports the claim behind it. Abbott's 2026 cash returned to shareholders is rebuilt from what it has filed for nine months plus the fourth-quarter dividend ($5.6B, was $5.2B). Several paths had no source that looks forward: the Nutrition category rates and how much of the US infant-formula gain came from WIC contracts, the growth of rapid and molecular tests, and how fast Devices R&D and selling costs grow. Their booked values stay as placeholders and go to Kilian as three new cards, each with its sourced options and engine-sized effect (all under 1.2%). The spinal cord stimulator market forecast is replaced by a newer edition (7.9% a year), and the searches for newer editions of the other outside forecasts are recorded. Old text that still quoted superseded multiples and settlement amounts is brought in line with the booked numbers. Research target (12m) base 109.78 -> 109.82 (+0.04%). Citation-gate fix round 4 (2026-11-18): currency effects are now built from forward exchange rates (interest-rate differentials against the Fed funds rate) for every business's foreign sales, not just EPD and Nutrition. Emerging-market currencies (rupee, real, peso, ruble, yuan) imply about -4.4% translation in 2027 and -5.1% a year after, which slows EPD to about 2.4% a year and turns Nutrition slightly negative; euro/yuan/yen/pound (weighted by Abbott's 10-K country sales) imply -1.0% in 2027 and +1.2% a year after for Devices and Diagnostics. Libre CGM 2027 now sits at the middle of the CEO's range (+3.5% before currency); the extra point for the formulary change and Libre Duo had no sized source and is a new card. Core Lab 2027-29 grows 3% a year (Roche's mid-term outlook, the only forward source) instead of Roche's past 5%, on the dx_base card. Each past quarterly EPS guide now cites the release that gave it; the CEO's early 2027 sales view ('pretty similar to this year') has its own check, and ours is below it. Research target (12m) base 109.82 -> 108.19. Citation-gate fix round 5 (2026-11-18): The fourth quarter of 2025 is taken out of Abbott's quarterly EPS-guide record, because Abbott never gave a guide for that quarter (the 1.47-1.53 range was our own arithmetic); the record is now 6 of 6 quarters inside the guide. For the fourth quarter of 2026, nothing Abbott said on the Q3 call sizes Core Lab, rapid and molecular tests, the segment margins or corporate costs. Core Lab now grows 3% (Roche's forward outlook, the same as 2027-29) instead of Roche's past 5%. The rapid and molecular placeholder, the Q4 segment margins and Q4 corporate costs stay placeholders and go to Kilian on cards; Q4 corporate costs are now the 2026 average quarter (-$65M) instead of an average Q4 share that changes sign from year to year (new corp card). Established Pharmaceuticals now grows 6.3% a year before currency, the forecast growth of the global branded-generics market, instead of the CEO's past 7.5-8% record. International infant formula now grows 7.7% before currency, the forecast growth of the infant nutrition market, which the CEO's statement that Nutrition volume will grow well above peers supports. Neuromodulation was booked at +1.1% a year, the Q3 decline of 1.1% with the sign flipped and no build behind it; it is now built by region (US at the Q3 pace of -5.6%, international at the stimulator market's 7.9%) for about -2.0% a year, still pending Kilian. Exact's 2027 growth is now 13.3%, with each part sourced (Cologuard mid-teens less one point for blood tests, the rest at the tumor-profiling market's 10.6%). For Libre in 2027, building growth from the CGM market forecasts (global 10.1%, or US 18.2% with the rest of the world implied) gives 8.9-10.1%; those builds assume Abbott keeps its share at today's prices, which the CEO's international price cuts contradict, so they are on the card but not booked. The 2027 sales check now also reads the CEO's expected acceleration; our build is below both readings. None of the evidence-based alternatives moves the research target (12m) by more than 5%. Research target (12m) base 108.19 -> 107.88 (-0.3%). Citation-gate fix round 6 (2026-11-18): For Libre in 2027 the set had stretched the CEO's 'low to mid-single digit' range for the fourth quarter over the whole year. That range is for Q4 and the next few quarters, and his only words on 2027 point higher ('Would I be surprised that we would do much better than that next year? It would not surprise me at all that we would do better.'). 2027 is now built from the market forecasts: the US at the global CGM market's 10.1% (not the 18.2% US forecast, which assumes Medicare coverage the CEO is not counting on), the rest of the world at the 2.6% that the two forecasts imply, less Abbott's own price cuts abroad. No one sizes those cuts, so they are sized at the slowdown from Q3 to the middle of the Q4 range, over two quarters. That gives +4.0% before currency, a little above the old 3.5%; it goes to Kilian on the card. Electrophysiology now grows with the newest market forecast, 14.9% a year (Mordor, September 2026, in line with Medtronic's 'mid-teens'), with no share gain booked, instead of an unsourced 13% market plus 2 points of share in 2027 and a fade to 11.5%. Heart failure grows 7.5% a year, the lower of the two market forecasts it spans (heart pumps 8.4%, heart-failure monitors 7.5%), instead of an unexplained 6%. Every Nutrition line now has a market forecast: US infant formula 5.0% (Renub, April 2026), US adult 5.6% and international adult 5.3% (Mordor, September 2026), so Nutrition grows about 3% a year instead of shrinking slightly; the part of Q3's US infant formula growth that comes from contract wins is now 6 points instead of 11. Exact's 2028-29 growth is now stated part by part (Cologuard at the 13.2% screening market less 2 points for blood tests, which goes to Kilian on a new card; the rest at 10.6%). The IVL market behind the SonicForce value now grows 15.8% a year (GMI) instead of a cut to a past quarter's pace. Several stale lines were brought up to date, the IQVIA '$121Bn' figure that the cited page does not show was dropped, and the Roche outlook is no longer called 'mid-term', because the page gives no timeframe. None of the evidence-based alternatives moves the research target (12m) by more than 5%. Research target (12m) base 107.88 -> 109.04 (+1.1%). Citation-gate fix round 7 (2026-11-18): The Q3 release says Libre and other glucose monitors grew 7.7% comparable in the quarter itself, so the slowdown into the fourth quarter (to about 3.5%) is bigger than the set had used. That slowdown is how Abbott's price cuts abroad are sized: about 7 points off international growth, and half of it carried into 2027. The 2027 build had mixed two publishers (one for the world market, another for the US), which made the implied rest-of-world rate inconsistent; it now uses one publisher's world and US figures together (Fortune Business Insights: 10.1% a year, US about 40% of the market), so the US and the rest of the world both grow 10.1% before Abbott's price cuts. Libre grows about 8% in 2027 before currency and 10.1% a year in 2028-29. The note on why the Mordor pair is not used now says what its page shows: its 2025 base is already overtaken by Abbott's 2026 actual sales. Rates that had been held from past periods now come from forward sources: Vascular grows 4.3% a year (Mordor's coronary stent and peripheral vascular forecasts, July 2026) and Rapid and Molecular diagnostics 5% a year (the low end of Roche's outlook). Exact's Cologuard grows with the 13.2% screening market in 2028-29, without the 2-point haircut that no source sized (2- and 4-point haircuts stay on the card).
